sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Single Arm Landmine Press Standing is a unilateral pressing exercise performed with one end of a barbell anchored in a landmine attachment or corner.

This unique pressing angle combines elements of both a shoulder press and an incline chest press, making it an excellent functional movement.

The single arm variation helps to identify and correct strength imbalances between sides while heavily engaging the core for stabilisation.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Unilateral movement corrects strength imbalances between sides
- Unique pressing angle reduces shoulder stress compared to overhead pressing
- Heavy core and anti-rotation demands improve stability
- Combines shoulder and upper chest activation
- Joint-friendly arc of motion follows a natural pressing path
- Standing position engages the entire kinetic chain
- Great for athletes requiring rotational power and stability
- Can be loaded progressively with standard weight plates

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Anterior Deltoids (Front Shoulders), Upper Pectoralis Major (Upper Chest)

Secondary: Triceps Brachii, Serratus Anterior, Core (Obliques and Transverse Abdominis), Trapezius

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Use a landmine attachment or position a barbell securely into the corner of a machine.
2. Stand facing the end of the barbell with feet shoulder-width apart.
3. Pick up the end of the barbell and hold it at shoulder height with one hand.
4. Position the barbell in a front rack position at the shoulder.
5. Keep your core braced and your back straight.
6. Stagger your feet slightly for additional stability if needed.
7. Keep your elbow tucked close to your body.
8. Ensure a firm grip on the end of the barbell.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Brace your core and maintain a straight back position.
2. Extend your arm and press the barbell overhead and to the front of your body.
3. Push through the movement until your arm is fully extended.
4. Keep your torso stable and resist rotation throughout the press.
5. Lower the bar back down slowly to the shoulder and front rack position.
6. Maintain control of the weight throughout the entire movement.
7. Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other shoulder.
8. Breathe out as you press up, breathe in as you lower the bar.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Excessive rotation of the torso during the press
- Leaning too far back or arching the lower back
- Not bracing the core throughout the movement
- Using momentum to push the weight up
- Flaring the elbow too far out from the body
- Not fully extending the arm at the top
- Rushing the eccentric (lowering) phase
- Uneven reps or loading between sides

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Olympic Barbell
- Landmine Attachment or Corner Setup
- Weight Plates
- Optional: Lifting Gloves (for grip comfort)
- Optional: Fat Grip Attachment (for increased grip challenge)

sections.heading: Landmine Setup
sections.content:
1. Secure a landmine attachment to a squat rack or heavy base.
2. Alternatively, wedge one end of the barbell into the corner of two walls or a machine.
3. Load the free end of the barbell with the desired weight plates.
4. Ensure the anchored end is stable and will not slip during the movement.
5. Test with light weight first to confirm the setup is secure.
6. Position yourself facing the free end of the barbell.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet shoulder-width apart, slight stagger optional.
2. Grip: One hand gripping the end of the barbell at shoulder height.
3. Elbow: Tucked close to the body in the starting position.
4. Core: Braced and tight throughout the movement.
5. Back: Straight and neutral, avoid excessive arching.
6. Shoulders: Packed down, avoid shrugging.
7. Knees: Slightly bent for stability.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Barbell Overhead Press: Bilateral overhead pressing movement
- Arnold Press: Rotational dumbbell pressing targeting all deltoid heads
- Dumbbell Shoulder Press: Bilateral or unilateral overhead pressing
- Push Press: Explosive overhead press using leg drive
- Cable Single Arm Press: Constant tension unilateral pressing

sections.heading: Landmine Variations
sections.content:
Single Arm Landmine Press Standing: Standard unilateral standing press
Double Arm Landmine Press: Both hands pressing together
Landmine Kneeling Press: Half-kneeling for increased core demand
Landmine Squat to Press: Full body compound movement
Landmine Rotational Press: Adding rotation for athletic power

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Shoulder Pain: Try a more neutral pressing angle or reduce range of motion
Lower Back Issues: Perform in a half-kneeling position for more stability
Grip Issues: Use lifting gloves or a fat grip attachment
No Landmine Attachment: Wedge the barbell into a corner securely
Beginner: Start with just the bar to learn the movement pattern
Core Weakness: Use a split stance for better stability
